title: Check a shared-resource rule for a double standard

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Fairness can require different treatment for a relevant constraint. It does not require ignoring disability access, nor using friendship or status as an unexplained advantage.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Room slots are 09–10,10–11,11–12. Rule agreed before requests: honor confirmed bookings; among new eligible requests use order received, while accommodating a documented time restriction where a feasible swap preserves others’ needs. Dana already has 09–10. Friend Eli requested either remaining slot at 08:00. Unfamiliar Fran requested only 10–11 at 08:05 because an agreed accessible transport return leaves 11:00. High-status Gus requested either at 08:10. No extra slot exists.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Allocate the slots, explain whose request remains unmet and exchange Eli/Fran’s names without changing circumstances. State what a role reversal does and does not show.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: Two applicants have identical needs and timing; one is your ally. An agreed lottery applies. May you bypass it because you trust the ally?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Dana keeps 09–10; Fran uses 10–11; Eli uses 11–12; Gus remains unallocated. Eli’s earlier request still receives a feasible slot, and the restriction explains Fran’s placement. Partial: correct allocation justified only by sympathy. Incorrect: favor Gus’s status or give the friend both remaining slots. A different rule needs actual agreement, not retrospective invention.
criteria: The same rule survives name exchange
Scarcity and the unserved person remain visible

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No supplied relevant difference supports bypassing the agreed lottery. Follow the process or openly seek a justified prospective rule change; personal familiarity is not the declared criterion.
